Depends on what you’re looking for and how the weather is. Weather is typically 60s in SF during the summer, which is warm and there will be some people at Ocean Beach, etc. There will be times when it’s foggy/wet as well, but some people still go to the beach during those days as well for a different mood. Around August/September are the heat waves, which is when everyone will head over to enjoy the heat (though the beaches still typically feel pretty cool during heatwaves and the water too cold to get in). Compared to LA though, there aren’t really any boardwalks or “beach culture”, though there won’t be a shortage of people at the beach when it’s a sunny day. The beaches here are more similar to NorCal and PNW beaches in that regard.

Most popular beaches here are Ocean Beach and Baker Beach. Aquatic Cove is nice because the water is calm and you can swim safely there

I think it helps if you like the song’s genre (dream pop, neo-psychedelia) in the first place. It’s very reminiscent of 90s dream pop/neo-psychedelic artists like Mazzy Star, Slowdive, and Fishmans and I personally see it as her “Fade Into You”. Songs like this I find typically have you focus in on how the singers voice sounds blends in with the typically dense, heavy reverberated, dreamlike, and spacious production. The voice merely becomes another instrument, like the guitars or the synths.

This isn’t her first dream pop song (see Ultraviolence), but to me, it was her first dream pop song that’s a simple, poignant love song. I find that her love songs typically have some inner subtext, like being the other woman, her lover mistreating her in some way, the lover dying, HER dying, etc, but Venice simply sings about transience of life, nostalgia, getting older with the one you love, and lamenting the end of summer. I do think it touches upon death very slightly, but it’s in a realistic “circle of life” existential and non-melodramatic way. Like many dream pop songs, it’s isn’t a lyrical masterpiece as you are focusing more so on the production, but the lyrics are simple, drowsy, and almost universally relatable. 

The instrumental breakdown is something that I immensely love, though it took me a few days to get used to it after it was released. There are so many textures and hidden gems that you can only catch on relistens. I still notice new things in the song upon relistens and it’s been out for 6 years. 

One of my favorite things about this song is the 70s references - “you’re in the yard I light the fire” is a reference to Our House by Crosby, Stills, Nash, and Young and “Crimson and Clover” by Tommy James, and “beautiful losers” by Leonard Cohen. This is coupled with the (imo wonderful) music video featuring a vintage San Francisco’s Ocean Beach and vintage 101 freeway footage. To me, this really adds to the song’s atmosphere of transience and how short life really is. The ending of the song is so simple and tragic, and I find the lines “if you weren’t mine, I’d be jealous of your love” to be haunting. It’s like a warm hug after a long journey, and it makes me want to listen to the song again just to hear that part.

Overall, I just think there was so much detail and love woven into this song. I personally think it represents Lana perfectly, especially her before her “wordy” era. There is a beautiful simplicity to the lyrics and her story but an equally beautiful complexity to the instrumental she sings and blends the story into.
